_comment: AM peak demand profiles for chi-loop-urban, as fractions of each flow's
peak-hour rate. 600 s steps x 9 = 5400 s = 54,000 ticks at dt=0.1.
Shapes differ by TRIP PURPOSE, which is the point: a single global curve
makes freight peak with commuters and sends the reverse-commute direction
downtown at the same moment as the inbound direction. Fractions are
napkin-anchored to the usual diurnal shapes, NOT calibrated counts -- the
same posture as every other rate in this scenario.
All four end in zeros so the network drains with arrivals off. Whether
congestion clears during that tail is what separates a loaded network

assign._why: Residents leaving downtown towers are largely counter-peak: they are already in the core, so they are not what fills the inbound expressways.
Interior mainline injections carry the freight mix (see mkod.py's ramp block), and freight peaks earlier and flatter than commuting.
